title: Tunisian mesh stitch market bag
excerpt: An open mesh market bag worked in DK cotton using Tunisian mesh stitch. The bag holds its shape while remaining stretchy enough for shopping trips.
sourceNotes: Tunisian mesh stitch creates an open grid by pairing yarn-overs with skipped bars on every forward pass, producing a light, stretchy fabric well suited to bags.

glossaryTerms.definition: Worked by alternating a yarn-over with a skipped bar on every forward pass, creating a grid of open eyelets across the fabric.
A thin rope of crochet worked by chaining a length and slip-stitching back along it to form a round, firm strap.

crochet.gaugeText: 16 sts x 12 rows = 10 cm in Tunisian mesh stitch on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 30 cm wide x 35 cm deep (excluding handles).

content.text: throughout. The bag is worked flat, seamed at the sides, and finished with simple

Chain 50. Row 1: pick up a loop in each chain (50 loops). Return pass. Row 2 (mesh): pick up first bar, *yarn over, skip 1 bar, pick up next bar; repeat from * to last bar, pick up last bar. Return pass. Repeat row 2 until each panel measures 35 cm. Bind off.
Place panels with wrong sides together. Using the tapestry needle, seam both side edges and across the bottom with a whip stitch.
For each handle, chain 70. Slip stitch back along each chain to form a firm cord. Attach each end of the cord securely to the bag top, spacing them 10 cm apart. Weave in all ends.
